Prime Minister Andy Burnham has announced a 10-year plan to improve UK high streets, including stricter planning laws for vape shops and betting centers to combat 'hollowed out' town centers.

The Poison:
The policy relies on increased regulation rather than economic support, which may accelerate the closure of small businesses struggling with high costs.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
The error is in the Q5 (HOW) plane: The government assumes planning control is the solution, ignoring the economic reality that businesses need tax relief to survive.

Social Physics Analysis:
By focusing on top-down regulation, the government maintains a control-based loop. True empowerment would involve addressing the business rates that drive out legitimate retailers.

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Reckoning. Regulatory tinkering without economic reform leads to systemic failure.

The Unavoidable Truth: High streets are struggling due to complex economic shifts, not just bad tenants.

The Unavoidable Lie: That local councils can regulate their way back to prosperity without fiscal support.
